subject: Procurement & buying channel next steps for Finovate — PO vs Marketplace
messages:

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.in>

Subject: Procurement & buying channel next steps for Finovate — PO vs Marketplace

Hi Maya / Finovate procurement team — thanks again for the call just now. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement path and timeline: 

What we covered (recap):
- Use case: embedding-based knowledge search for customer support (production pilot Q3).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~1M tokens/day, burst to 2–3x.
- Risk profile: need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and contract with data processing terms.

Commercial/Procurement options discussed:
1) Direct PO (Redwood invoice -> Finovate PO) — preferred for enterprise terms, custom SLA, and flexible billing cadence.
2) AWS Marketplace — faster procurement in some orgs; billing consolidated via AWS invoice; vendor onboarding on AWS side required and may constrain custom SLA language.
3) Card / self-service — possible for pilot but not ideal for long-term commitments at this scale.

What we need from you to qualify path:
- Confirm which channel you prefer for the pilot (Card / Direct PO / AWS Marketplace).
- If PO: estimated internal PO processing lead time and any required PO template.
- If Marketplace: confirm AWS account owner and whether you require private offers or marketplace listing.
- List of compliance docs needed for vendor onboarding (SOC2, DPA, pen test).

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_packet.pdf (contains SOC2 summary, DPA, company info), SLA-summary.xlsx (high-level SLA options).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Maya: can you confirm procurement channel preference and expected PO timeline by end of next week (EOD Thu 4/8)?
- Sean: I left the pricing options in the packet; can you add a short note about differences we should flag for marketplace vs PO?
- I’ll loop legal if you need customized terms or a redline.

Thanks — happy to set a short follow-up with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Subject: Re: Procurement & buying channel next steps for Finovate — PO vs Marketplace

Thanks, Stephanie — solid recap. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- For enterprise deals like this we generally prefer Direct PO (finance processes POs monthly). That said, we are open to AWS Marketplace if it speeds procurement, provided the listing supports a private/negotiated offer so our legal can accept the DPA changes.
- Typical PO processing time is ~3 weeks (from receipt of the formal quote + vendor onboarding completion). If vendor onboarding requires AWS MOL (Marketplace Onboarding Lifecycle) it can add 2–4 weeks depending on AWS schedules.
- Required docs: SOC2 Type II report, DPA, vendor contact for security questionnaire, and a billing remittance address.

Would you be able to send a formal quote/estimate and a short summary of the marketplace onboarding implications? Also please point me to the PO instructions we need to give to finance (remit to, invoice cadence, tax info).

Appreciate the packet — I’ll share with our legal and loop back.

Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement | Finovate LLC

Thanks for the context, Maya — quick technical/commercial notes from my side to help you choose the channel: 

- Marketplace vs PO: functionally both work for serving traffic; the differences are operational:
  * AWS Marketplace (private offer): typically faster to get purchasing approved by your finance team, billing consolidates onto your AWS invoice. However, private offers do have an AWS vendor onboarding step and can limit custom SLA language — we can request a private offer that references Redwood’s DPA but legal sometimes prefers direct contract.
  * Direct PO: allows us to accept Finovate-specific SLA/penalty language and shorter-term pilot billing cadence. Billing is direct to your AP contact and we can issue invoices per the PO schedule.
- Timeline assumptions: if you want pilot ready in June, Direct PO with initial paperwork this month is safest. Marketplace could work if your AWS onboarding team can turn private offer within 2–3 weeks.

What I can provide next:
- A formal line-item quote (PDF) suitable for PO.
- A short note on marketplace private offer steps and an estimated onboarding timeline.
- A contact at our partnerships team who handles marketplace listings (if you want to route through them).

If helpful I can draft the quote today and drop it in the shared Drive link.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
